pairs.registryProposal: Upward lesson for reduced-motion-mechanics. The technique's liveness rule stops at 'subscribe, and where the platform's own reader does not subscribe, wrap it' — which is the right shape for a React consumer but leaves a scripted frame engine one rung short. rafAnimationEngine.ts:53-58 and :89-92 record the failure the subscribe rule does not catch: the preference was sampled at target-set time, so turning it on mid-flight left the current travel running to completion, and an entry whose target never moved again never re-read it at all. The fix they landed — re-evaluate the merged signal once per frame inside the loop, before any physics runs, so the resolved end state arrives on the very next frame — is a third liveness shape worth naming in the technique alongside the subscription, with its cost stated (one matchMedia read per frame, only while something is animating).
